# AI Agent Engineering — The 10 Principles of determinism

> Markdown (GEO/AEO) version of <https://mauricio.issei.com.br/en/engenharia-agentes-ia>. Author: **Maurício Yokoyama Issei** · en-BR · Published: 2026-06-10 · Updated: 2026-06-21.

## In short

**AI Agent Engineering** is the discipline of building reliable agentic systems treating the output of the model as **unreliable input** governed by architecture. The central rule: a reliable AI system has **Very little AI on the critical path** — rules and data solve the deterministic and the model only acts on the interpretive residue.

- **Deterministic-first** — settle with rules and data; spend AI only where the model is irreplaceable.
- **Brain × display** — separate cognitive (sensitive) motor from the interface (exposed) by a narrow contract.
- **Rigid Contracts + Insurance Threshold** — strict schema rejects unexpected fields and confidence below the floor; fail-closed.
- **MCP + FinOps per ledger** — controlled tool border and quota refusing expenditure before provider.

## The Invariant Principle

A reliable AI system has very little AI on the critical path. Confidence is not born of a smarter prompt, but of more disciplined architecture: rules and data solve the deterministic and the model is called only in the interpretive residue, under contracts that make its output auditable.

## Borders

Rigid contracts across borders turn the probabilistic output of the LLM into validated input. The MCP standardizes agent tools; the quota ledger governs the cost; the Clearing Threshold with fail-closed ensures that nothing below the trusted floor becomes a fact.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is AI Agent Engineering?**

It is the discipline of designing reliable agentic systems treating each model output as unreliable input, validated by architecture (schemes, thresholds, borders). The objective is to keep little AI in the critical path: rules and data solve the deterministic and LLM acts only on the interpretive residue.

**What does "deterministic-first" mean?**

Solve with structured rules and data everything possible and reserve the AI only for the fraction of the task that requires the model. Same entry must produce the same output; non-determinism is isolated and testable.

**What is Brain separation × display?**

The cognitive motor (heavy, with access to sensitive data) and the exposed interface are separate systems, connected by a narrow contract. The display never touches the bank directly; the brain never blindly trusts what comes from outside — reduces the surface of attack and failure.

**What's the surety threshold and fail-closed?**

Every inference carries a degree of confidence; the architecture defines a floor below which the output is intercepted before turning fact and degraded to a structured fallback (human revision, explicit uncertainty or deterministic route). If it was not possible to conclude safely, the system stops at a safe place instead of promoting a hunch.

**What is the role of the MCP (Model Context Protocol)?**

The MCP is the security border by which the agent gains "hands and eyes" in a controlled manner, explicitly declaring which tools he can use. Each tool is typed by a schema with pre and post-conditions, which makes the actions of the agent auditable.

**How to control cost (FinOps) in AI agents?**

With a quota ledger: a persistent domain state that governs credits and spent and refuses expense before even calling the provider. Combined with early pruning (cheap filter first), it prevents the cost of calls to models from escaping control.

## Glossary

- **Deterministic-first** — Solve with rules and data; spend AI only on interpretive residue.
- **Brain × display** — Separation between cognitive motor (sensitive) and interface (exposed), connected by narrow contract.
- **Rigid contract (scheme)** — Strict scheme that rejects unexpected fields and inferences below the Clearing Threshold.
- **Sure Threshold** — Trust floor below which inference is intercepted and degraded to structured fallback.
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** — Protocol giving the agent controlled and declared tools (safety border).
- **Quota Ledger** — Persistent state that governs spent/credits and refuses expense before provider (FinOps).
- **Open-World** — Absence of data is explicit uncertainty, never "false".
- **Fail-closed** — If it was not possible to conclude safely, stop at a safe place instead of promoting a hunch.
